title: Events Administrator
description:
Job Title: Events Administrator

Location: Liverpool Street, London
Pay: 14-16 per hour

Duration: 2 months minimum
Hours: Monday-Friday, 37.5-40 hours per week
Start Date: ASAP

What you'll be doing
- Manage and respond to enquiries received through the shared Events inbox.
- Process event bookings and maintain accurate event records and attendee data.
- Support the preparation and packing of event materials prior to events.
- Unpack, organise, and reconcile materials following events.
- Conduct regular stock checks and maintain inventory records.
- Coordinate courier bookings and liaise with delivery providers regarding event logistics.
- Arrange and manage event printing requirements.
- Create event collateral, including posters, speaker cards, signage, and delegate materials.
- Set up event surveys and assist with compiling post-event reports.
- Collect printed materials from suppliers and carry out quality and accuracy checks.
- Proofread event communications and printed materials.
- Provide basic marketing and promotional support for events.
- Assist the wider Events Team with day-to-day administration and coordination activities.
- Undertake additional ad hoc administrative duties as required.

What you'll bring
- Previous experience within events administration, events coordination, office administration, or marketing support.
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail.
- Able to manage multiple priorities and work effectively to deadlines.
- A confident communicator, both written and verbal.
- Comfortable liaising with suppliers, couriers, colleagues, and external stakeholders.
- Proactive, reliable, and capable of working independently.
- Flexible and willing to support hands-on event preparation activities.
- A collaborative team player with a positive and adaptable approach.
- Competent in Microsoft Office, including Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
- Experienced in working with spreadsheets, databases, and administrative systems.
- Confident producing accurate written communications and proofreading documents
- Experience supporting event logistics and delivery.
- Knowledge of booking systems, CRM systems, or event management platforms would be advantageous.

title: Administrator
description:
Administrator
- Location: Liverpool City Centre
- Salary: 26,000 per annum
- Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am - 5:00pm
- Type: Full-Time, Permanent

About the Role

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an organised and detail-oriented Administrator to join a well-established organisation within the rehabilitation and injury management sector.

Working from modern offices in Liverpool City Centre, you will play a key role in supporting both clinical diary management and general office administration. This position would suit someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys coordinating schedules, and takes pride in delivering excellent administrative support.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing and coordinating clinician diaries and appointments
- Scheduling patient consultations to maximise clinician availability
- Resolving diary conflicts and managing schedule changes
- Liaising with internal teams, referral companies, and external stakeholders
- Maintaining accurate records using Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and Outlook
- Supporting supplier management and maintaining strong working relationships
- Researching and sourcing appropriate rehabilitation providers based on client requirements
- Managing Data Protection inboxes and associated actions
- Assisting with general office administration duties

Additional Duties
- Ordering office stationery and supplies
- Handling incoming and outgoing post
- Booking hotels and travel arrangements
- Greeting visitors and providing a professional front-of-house service
- Organising courier bookings and collections
- Supporting the wider team with ad hoc administrative tasks

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous administration experience
- Excellent organisational and time management skills
- Strong attention to detail
- Confidence using Microsoft Office packages, particularly Word, Excel, and Outlook
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing demands
- A professional and confidential approach to handling sensitive information

What's on Offer?
- Salary of 26,000 per annum
- Monday to Friday working hours, 9am - 5pm
- Liverpool City Centre location
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- Opportunity to develop within a growing and established business

If you're looking for an administration role where no two days are the same and you can make a real impact within a busy and supportive team, we'd love to hear from you.

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

title: Project Administrator
description:
Project Administrator

Project Administrator Desirable

title: Business Support Co-ordinator
description:
Business Support Co-ordinator

Join the Team at Gaskells (North West) Ltd

Are you highly organised, customer-focused and thrive in a fast-paced environment? Do you enjoy solving problems, building relationships and supporting a busy sales team? If so, we'd love to hear from you.

We are looking for a Business Support Co-ordinator to join our growing team and play a key role in delivering excellent customer service, supporting our Business Development Managers and ensuring our customers receive a seamless experience. The role focuses on contract processing, supply chain support and customer excellence.

About the Role

As a Business Support Co-ordinator, you'll be the link between our customers, sales team and supply chain partners. You'll help manage customer contracts, resolve service issues, coordinate subcontracted services and ensure every customer receives an outstanding level of support.

No two days are the same, so we're looking for someone who enjoys variety, takes ownership of their work and is passionate about delivering great service.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide exceptional customer service via telephone and email.
- Support Business Development Managers with customer enquiries, contracts and day-to-day administration.
- Process contracts accurately and efficiently.
- Build strong relationships with customers, suppliers and colleagues.
- Resolve customer and subcontractor service issues quickly and professionally.
- Ensure subcontracted services are delivered smoothly and in line with customer expectations.
- Use business systems including CRM, Microsoft Office and reporting software to maintain accurate records.
- Provide contract information and support to the sales team.
- Ensure customer solutions comply with environmental, safety and regulatory requirements.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who is:
- Customer focused with an excellent telephone manner.
- Positive, resilient and confident.
- Adaptable with a willingness to learn.
- A natural problem solver who can think on their feet.
- Organised with excellent attention to detail.
- Calm under pressure and able to manage competing priorities.
- Professional with strong communication and relationship-building skills.

Essential Skills & Experience
- Excellent customer communication skills.
- Strong organisational skills.
- Strong conflict resolution and problem-solving abilities.
- Good PC skills, including Microsoft Office.
- Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Ability to negotiate and build lasting customer relationships.

Desirable
- Experience using CRM or sales management systems.
- Experience within the waste management or environmental sector.

Why Join Gaskells?

At Gaskells, we pride ourselves on delivering exceptional service while creating a supportive and professional working environment. We value:

Teamwork

Customer excellence

Professionalism

Honesty and integrity

Continuous learning and development

Respect for colleagues and the environment

Apply Today

If you're looking for an opportunity where your organisational skills, customer service expertise and positive attitude can make a real difference, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and become part of a team that's committed to delivering outstanding service every day.

Please include your CV and a short covering email explaining why you would be a great fit for the Business Support Co-ordinator role.

- Excellent customer service and communication skills

- The ability to manage multiple priorities in a busy environment
- Previous experience managing social media for a business
- Experience creating content across Facebook, Instagram and TikTok
- Knowledge of Meta Business Suite
- Experience using Canva or similar design tools
- Strong written communication skills
- A positive, solutions-focused approach
- The confidence to work independently and use initiative

- Full UK driving licence

What's on Offer?

title: Clerical Officer
company: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
description: The post will be based primarily at the Royal Liverpool Hospital and will support services delivered across Liverpool University Hospitals sites, including Aintree and Woodlands Hospice. The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring that referrals, enquiries and clinical information are managed accurately, efficiently and in accordance with Trust procedures. The post holder will need to work effectively as part of a busy administrative team, demonstrating excellent communication, organisational and prioritisation skills. The post holder will be expected to maintain confidentiality, exercise discretion and communicate professionally and sensitively with patients, relatives, carers and colleagues. Provide comprehensive administrative and clerical support to the Palliative Care and Acute Oncology clinical teams. Act as a point of contact for telephone and email enquiries, ensuring that queries are managed professionally and escalated where appropriate. Coordinate and process referrals, ensuring that information is recorded accurately and communicated to clinical colleagues in a timely manner. Enter, maintain and update patient and service information using relevant Trust systems and Microsoft Office applications, including Excel. Support the administration of the weekly Palliative Care MDT, including the preparation of information and follow-up of agreed actions where required. Provide administrative cross-cover to support service continuity during periods of planned and unplanned leave, as required.

title: Receptionist
description: Multiple vacancies have arisen for a motivated and enthusiastic person to work for the Walk in Centre team across the 4 Liverpool Sites; City Walk In, Smithdown Walk In, Garston UTC and Old Swan UTC. They will be customer focused and provide a comprehensive service. Communication and organisational skills are essential. Multiple vacancies full-time and part-time available. They must have excellent inter personal skills, and be able to organise and prioritise their work schedule. They must be able to work on their own initiative, with excellent telephone manner and respectful confidentiality. Previous experience is desirable . They must also be willing to work across all sites as required. You will be required to cover sickness and absence. The service is open daily 8am to 8pm including Bank Holidays (including Xmas Day), and weekends, and shifts are allocated according to service needs. The post holder will provide reception and administrative duties to ensure the smooth day to day running of the work environment. Work with colleagues in establishing and maintaining administrative procedures to promote patient satisfaction, respecting the confidential nature of information relating to the Trust, its staff and patients. To participate in training and development programmes both internal and externally. Ensure the delivery of the quality strategy within the designated area incorporating establishment of systems and processes. Receive and direct patients and visitors on arrival at the centre, providing reception services for patients, staff, public, internal and external customers and organisations ensuring sensitivity when dealing with distressing situations. Answering telephone calls using the switchboard system receive and process incoming and outgoing telephones calls, taking messages and responding appropriately to maintain effective communication channels. Sorting and distribution of mail to all departments. Manage and maintain stock levels and ordering supplies. Accurately record new and follow up attendances on the electronic appointment system, updating and revising information where necessary. Assisting with the collection of data and statistics to produce standardised computer generated reports and/or statistical information for managers as and when required. Maintain filing systems and other records as required ensuring they are up to date and accurate and implement changes to systems and procedures as directed. To participate in meetings as required. To ensure a professional approach to work maintaining confidentiality throughout. Generally monitor security within the building. Ensuring reception and waiting areas are kept clean, tidy and safe. Report and record sickness, absences and any incidents or accidents in accordance with Trust Policy. Staff may be required to work from other bases within the organisation.
